title: InvoiceRail — stablecoin invoices on QDay Aevum

slides.heading: The loop
slides.body: Issue an invoice in tUSD8, settle it in parts, withdraw whenever, cancel what expires.
slides.code:
createInvoice(id, 250e18, dueAt)
pay(id, 100e18)   // remaining 150
pay(id, 150e18)   // remaining 0
withdraw(id)      // merchant balance 250
cancel(id2)       // after expiry

slides.heading: What it refuses
slides.body: Overpayment, past-due payment, double settlement, partial withdrawal of more than is due, and anyone but the merchant.
slides.code:
require(balanceOf(payer) >= amount, "balance")
Overpay  -> revert
Past due -> revert
Settled  -> revert

slides.heading: The page
slides.body: A static page reads any deployment and settles invoices through the browser wallet.

slides.heading: Why balance deltas
slides.body: Transfers are checked by the change in the token's balance, so a fee-on-transfer token cannot make the books lie.

slides.heading: Thirteen tests
slides.body: Happy path, partial payments, overpay, expiry, cancellation, permissions, no-return token, unknown invoice, zero amount, duplicate id, and a full lifecycle transcript.
slides.code:
forge test
Ran 2 test suites: 13 tests passed, 0 failed

slides.heading: Proven on the testnet state
slides.body: The deploy and the full invoice lifecycle are simulated against the live Aevum chain before any gas is spent.
slides.code:
$ forge script script/Demo.s.sol:Demo --fork-url https://rpc-test.qday.info
  1. invoice created for 250 tUSD8, due in 7 days
  2. payer paid 100; remaining: 150
  3. payer paid the last 150; remaining: 0
  4. merchant withdrew: 250
  5. second invoice expired and was cancelled by the merchant
